title: Configuration program blocks
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-state Turing machine with $k$ work tapes, and let $n,T$ be natural numbers. Let $\ell$ be a list of bit sources, each of which is either an input bit with index less than $n$, a Boolean constant, or a bit of a block with index less than $0$ and bit index less than the configuration width; let $x$ be any Boolean list. For every index $i$ within the configuration program, its computed block is the configuration expansion at index $i$, evaluated on the input obtained by evaluating each source in $\ell$ against $x$ and the empty list of prior blocks.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite-state Turing machine over Boolean symbols
Every source in $\ell$ is valid for input width $n$, configuration width, and instruction index $0$
$i$ is less than the configuration program length
